title: STAGE: Non-Linear AR Task Guidance via Dependency Modeling

publications.title: Dependency-Aware AR Guidance for Replaying Non-Linear Work

summary: STAGE converts expert AR recordings into a dependency graph of task segments, letting users replay procedural work non-linearly while respecting the constraints that link steps. The system segments multimodal video, gaze, and motion data into meaningful units and models their dependencies as a directed acyclic graph, supporting flexible workflows where strict step-by-step sequences are insufficient.
full_description: This project introduces STAGE, a system that transforms expert AR recordings into structured, replayable task guidance using a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG). Instead of linear video playback, it segments multimodal data (video, gaze, motion) into meaningful task units and models their dependencies. The system enables users to navigate tasks non-linearly while respecting procedural constraints. It aims to support flexible, real-world workflows where strict step-by-step sequences are insufficient.
key_result: Models task steps and their dependencies as a DAG so guidance can be replayed non-linearly.

title: Location-based Non-linear Playback of AR Task Recording

publication.title: Location-Based Non-Linear Playback of AR Task Recording

summary: A non-linear replay approach automatically segments AR task recordings by spatial location, so reviewers can jump directly to the task segment associated with their current physical position rather than scrubbing a timeline. In a user study with 19 participants, 89.5% preferred the location-based interface and reported reduced mental and physical demand relative to conventional linear playback.
full_description: This project investigates a non-linear replay approach that automatically segments AR task recordings based on spatial location data. Instead of manual timeline scrubbing, the system enables reviewers to jump directly to task segments associated with their current physical location. A user study with 19 participants found that 89.5% preferred the location-based interface, reporting reduced mental and physical demand compared to conventional linear playback.
key_result: A user study with 19 participants found that 89.5% preferred the location-based interface, reporting reduced mental and physical demand compared to conventional linear playback.

title: Focus-Aware AR Guidance: Adaptive Playback via Gaze and Location

publication.title: Focus-Aware Task Guidance: Adaptive AR Instruction Playback Via Gaze and Location Tracking

summary: Focus-aware AR guidance adapts to user attention using gaze and spatial context. By detecting whether a user is engaged, distracted, or lost, the system adjusts playback speed or pauses automatically. Results indicate adaptive guidance improves task accuracy and reduces manual control compared with static playback, and that well-chosen signals can outperform more complex multimodal combinations.
full_description: This project explores how AR guidance can dynamically adapt to user attention using gaze and spatial context. By detecting whether users are engaged, distracted, or lost, the system adjusts playback speed or pauses automatically. Results show that adaptive guidance improves task accuracy and reduces manual control compared to static playback. The work highlights how minimal, well-chosen signals can outperform more complex multi-modal combinations.
key_result: Adaptive guidance improves task accuracy and reduces manual control compared with static playback.

title: Spatial Guidance Cues in AR: Line vs. Radar Navigation

publication.title: Augmented Reality Spatial Guidance Cues for Flexible Multi-Objective Task Environments

summary: Spatial guidance cues are compared for AR navigation. Egocentric line-based guidance significantly improves efficiency, reduces head movement, and enhances spatial orientation relative to radar-based cues, while radar cues introduce additional cognitive load when mapping 2D representations into 3D space. The findings stress the importance of intuitive, embodied visual design in AR systems.
full_description: This project investigates how different visual guidance cues affect user navigation in AR environments. Comparing line-based and radar-based cues, the study finds that egocentric line guidance significantly improves efficiency, reduces head movement, and enhances spatial orientation. Radar cues, while informative, introduce additional cognitive load when mapping 2D representations to 3D space. The findings emphasize the importance of intuitive, embodied visual design in AR systems.
key_result: Egocentric line-based cues improve navigation efficiency and spatial orientation, while radar cues add cognitive load when mapping 2D representations to 3D space.

title: Adaptive Avatar Agents for Context-Aware VR Collaboration

publication.title: Adaptive Avatar Agents for Context-Aware VR Collaboration

summary: Adaptive avatar agents are investigated as attention guides and collaboration partners in VR. The system records head pose, hand interaction, objects, voice, and task duration, then applies speech-to-text, vision-language models, and text embeddings so agents can review and respond to user activity. Agents transform between human, robot, animal, and object forms based on conversation context, task state, and environmental events.
full_description: This project explores how AI-driven avatar agents can support attention guidance, task review, and collaboration in immersive VR environments. The system records user behaviour during VR tasks, including head position, head direction, hand interaction, grabbed objects, voice, and task duration, then uses speech-to-text, vision-language models, and text embeddings to help the agent review and respond to user activity. A key focus is adaptive avatar embodiment: the agent can transform between different avatar types, such as humans, robots, animals, fish, birds, and animated objects, based on conversation context, task state, environmental events, and possible biological signals. The project aims to investigate how avatar diversity, transformation, and environment-aware behaviour can make AI agents more expressive, noticeable, and useful in VR task guidance and collaborative scenarios.
key_result: A context-aware avatar agent system that records multimodal VR task behaviour and adapts its embodiment to the conversation and task state.

title: Facilitating Discussions in Immersive Virtual Meetings with Virtual Agents

publication.title: Facilitating Discussions in Immersive Virtual Meetings with Virtual Agents

summary: Proactive virtual agents are studied as facilitators in immersive virtual meetings. A cloud-based LLM service tracks agendas, transcripts, time remaining, and participant talk time, then facilitates by introducing agendas, keeping time, encouraging quieter participants, and summarising discussion. A user study comparing passive and active agent behaviours suggests proactive facilitation improves discussion support while requiring nuanced timing to avoid distraction.
full_description: This project investigates how proactive virtual agents can support collaboration in immersive virtual meetings. The system uses a cloud-based LLM service to track meeting agendas, transcripts, time remaining, and participant talk time, then provides timely facilitation such as introducing agendas, keeping time, encouraging quieter participants, and summarising discussion. A user study comparing passive and active agent behaviours suggests proactive facilitation can improve discussion support, while also requiring more nuanced timing to avoid distraction.
key_result: A proactive LLM-driven agent facilitates immersive meetings by managing agendas, time, and participation.

title: Gaze-Adaptive Diminished Reality for Attention Management
summary: Gaze-adaptive diminished reality is examined for managing visual attention in AR by selectively reducing irrelevant information. Two approaches are explored, binary visibility and multi-level transparency driven by gaze behaviour, with the system dynamically modulating scene visibility to guide attention without fully removing context. The work contributes to understanding how subtle visual suppression can support focus in complex environments.
full_description: This project examines how Diminished Reality (DR) can be used to manage visual attention in AR by selectively reducing irrelevant information. Two approaches are explored: binary visibility and multi-level transparency based on gaze behavior. The system dynamically modulates scene visibility to guide attention without fully removing context. This work contributes to understanding how subtle visual suppression can improve focus in complex environments.
key_result: Compares binary visibility and gaze-driven multi-level transparency for diminished-reality attention management in AR.

title: The Fusion Nexus: Biocognitive Audio-Verbal Interface in Asymmetric XR Collaboration

publication.title: The Fusion Nexus: Exploring the Confluence of Virtual and Real Worlds through Biocognitive Audio-Verbal Interface in Immersive XR Environments

summary: FusionNexus is an asymmetric XR collaboration experience in which a VR player guides a real-world player through pose-based tasks. A machine learning model performs real-time pose detection, while the VR player's heartbeat, captured with a Shimmer PPG sensor, controls drum tempo in the background music to convey emotional and physical state. Players collaborate on a timed challenge under immersive pressure.
full_description: FusionNexus is an asymmetric collaboration experience where a VR player guides a real-world player through pose-based tasks. A machine learning model performs real-time pose detection, while the VR player's heartbeat — captured via a Shimmer PPG sensor — controls drum beat tempo in background music, conveying emotional and physical state across realities. The two players collaborate to complete a timed challenge under immersive pressure.
key_result: An asymmetric XR experience linking real-time pose detection with heartbeat-driven audio to connect VR and real-world players.
